newsitem.title: USA: US FCC proposes to ease foreign satellite rules.
newsitem.headline: US FCC proposes to ease foreign satellite rules.

text.p: Federal regulators proposed Thursday to make it easier for foreign satellite operators to provide service in the United States if their home country has signed the recent global telecommunications accord.
The Federal Communications Commission proposal would implement provisions of the World Trade Organization (WTO) agreement liberalizing telecom markets around the globe.

Satellite operators whose home nations have signed the pact no longer would have to jump through a key regulatory hoop to get into business in the United States -- namely, an FCC ruling that the home country has opened its market to U.S. satellite operators.

But companies from nations who have not signed the WTO accord -- including Russia and China -- could be barred from the United states if their home country has not adequately opened its market to U.S. satellite companies.

Foreign providers of satellite-delivered television and radio, meanwhile, would be exempted from the FCC's proposed liberalizations. The United States exempted itself from key WTO provisions related to satellite TV and radio.
